1.title: By Command of God Our Savior
1.context: Paul signs himself an apostle by the command of God our Savior and of Christ Jesus our hope. Savior is this letter's characteristic title for God, and hope will carry the letter to its close.
1.question: What changes when you treat your work as a command received rather than a choice you made?

1.title: Grace, Mercy, and Peace
1.context: The greeting adds mercy to the usual grace and peace, the coworker letters' signature. The framing on Timothy's Ephesus posting and the charge ahead rides this scene.
1.question: Where do you need mercy standing between grace and peace in your own work right now?

2.title: Stay On at Ephesus
2.context: Timothy was urged, not ordered, to stay while Paul went to Macedonia. The certain men are already teaching; the confrontation is the posting.
2.question: What post are you holding right now mainly because someone you trust asked you to stay?

2.title: Myths and Endless Genealogies
2.context: The false material promotes speculation; God's work is a stewardship by faith. Endlessly extendable teaching never has to arrive anywhere.
2.question: What religious conversation in your life generates questions but never arrives anywhere?

2.title: The Goal Is Love
2.context: The goal of all the instruction is love from a pure heart, a clear conscience, and a sincere faith. Confrontation is measured by whether it grows this love.
2.question: How would your next hard conversation change if love, so defined, were its stated goal?

2.title: Teachers Who Do Not Understand
2.context: They strayed into empty talk and want to be teachers of the law without understanding what they so confidently assert. Ambition is named before error.
2.question: Where is your confidence loudest exactly where your understanding is thinnest?

3.title: Good, If Used Legitimately
3.context: The law is good when used for what it was given to do. The false teachers are rebuked for mishandling it, not for touching it.
3.question: What good tool, rule, or text have you seen do harm mainly through misuse?

3.title: Not Enacted for the Righteous
3.context: Law is addressed to lawbreakers, and the list begins by moving through the commandments in reverse image, from violence against parents to murder.
3.question: Which entry in the list surprises you most, and what does the surprise teach you?

3.title: Averse to Sound Teaching
3.context: The list ends by opening to anyone averse to sound teaching, tying the law's use to the glorious gospel entrusted to Paul. The testimony teaser rides this scene.
3.question: What does it mean to you that law and gospel agree rather than compete?

4.title: Considered Faithful
4.context: Paul thanks Christ for strengthening him, considering him faithful, and appointing him to service. His credential is a judgment made about him by Another.
4.question: Where has someone else's trust in you carried you further than your own record could?

4.title: Blasphemer, Persecutor, Violent Man
4.context: His three old titles match the law's list he just gave. Mercy came because he acted in ignorance and unbelief, ground for mercy, not an excuse of innocence.
4.question: What part of your own past do you still read as disqualifying that grace may read differently?

4.title: An Example of Perfect Patience
4.context: Grace overflowed, then the trustworthy saying, then the reason: his rescue is a display of perfect patience for everyone who would believe after him.
4.question: Who measures their hope by your case, and what do they see there?

4.title: To the King Eternal
4.context: The testimony ends in worship, not summary: the King eternal, immortal, invisible, the only God. The Amen closes the letter's first movement.
4.question: When did an honest look at your own rescue last end in worship rather than embarrassment?

5.title: By Them You May Fight
5.context: The command is entrusted to Timothy in keeping with the prophecies about him. His own history is issued as equipment for the good fight.
5.question: What word spoken over you earlier in your life is meant to be fought with now?

5.title: Shipwrecked Faith
5.context: Faith and a good conscience are the soldier's kit. Rejecting the conscience comes first in Paul's account; the faith wrecks after.
5.question: Is there a place where you are pushing your conscience away to keep something else afloat?

5.title: Handed Over to Be Taught
5.context: Hymenaeus and Alexander are carried as Paul names them, handed over to Satan with the stated purpose, to be taught not to blaspheme. The forward paragraph rides this scene.
5.question: How do you hold severity and hope together when someone you know wrecks their own faith?

6.title: For Kings and All in Authority
6.context: Four words for prayer are stacked and aimed at everyone, rulers named specifically. The aim is tranquil and quiet lives in godliness and dignity.
6.question: When did you last pray for a ruler you did not choose, and what did you ask for?

6.title: Who Wants Everyone to Be Saved
6.context: The praying matches God's stated desire: everyone saved and coming to the knowledge of the truth. The width of the prayer copies the width of the wanting.
6.question: Whose salvation have you quietly stopped expecting, and what would praying again look like?

6.title: One God, One Mediator
6.context: One God and one mediator, the man Christ Jesus, who gave himself as a ransom for all, the testimony given at just the right time.
6.question: What does it change in your praying that access runs through one mediator who paid, not a clerk who forwards?

6.title: I Am Not Lying
6.context: Paul insists on his appointment as teacher of the Gentiles with a double oath, suggesting the claim itself was contested at Ephesus.
6.question: When your calling is questioned, what do you state plainly and then move on from?

7.title: Holy Hands, Without Anger
7.context: The men's praying carries one condition twice over: holy hands, and no anger or dissension. The letter's fight is not inside the praying body.
7.question: What do you need to set down before your next prayer can honestly be prayed?

7.title: Adorned with Good Deeds
7.context: Adorn keeps its place in the sentence; Paul says what the adornment is: modesty, self-control, and positively, good deeds, proper for women who profess to worship God.
7.question: What would it look like for your visible life to be arranged around good deeds rather than impression?

7.title: Learn in Quietness
7.context: Learn stands first as a command. Verse 12 is carried exactly as written, in its setting, with no application argued in either direction in the telling.
7.question: How do you receive an instruction you find difficult: by softening it, extending it, or sitting with it as written?

7.title: Formed First, and Deceived
7.context: Paul grounds the instruction in his reading of Genesis, order and deception, told whole in the Genesis book of this series, where the seam can be weighed.
7.question: How carefully do you check the grounds given for an instruction before you accept or resist it?

7.title: If They Continue
7.context: The closing sentence is carried as written with no explanation invented; teachers have read it several ways for centuries. Its own condition is continuance in faith, love, holiness, and self-control.
7.question: Which of the four continuance words, faith, love, holiness, self-control, is your weakest right now?

8.title: A Noble Task
8.context: Aspiration toward oversight is called noble by a trustworthy saying. The list that follows is almost entirely character, and includes only one skill, able to teach.
8.question: What ambition in you is actually noble, and have you let yourself want it plainly?

8.title: Above Reproach
8.context: The character list is carried as written, including the husband of but one wife, hospitality as a requirement, and the negatives around wine, violence, and money.
8.question: Which single quality on the overseer list would your closest friends say is your weakest?

8.title: How Can He Care for the Church?
8.context: The household is the proving ground: management and care are the same work at two scales, and failure at the small scale is not promoted past.
8.question: What does your household management say about the care you could offer a larger flock?

8.title: A Good Reputation with Outsiders
8.context: Time is a qualification, since newness plus office swells into conceit. Outsiders' verdict counts as evidence, because disgrace in their eyes is a snare.
8.question: What do people who owe you nothing say about you, and do you treat it as evidence?

9.title: The Mystery of the Faith
9.context: Deacons' dignity runs to speech and appetite, not double-tongued, and inside they hold the mystery of the faith with a clear conscience, the delegate's own kit at servant rank.
9.question: Do the people you serve experience you as saying the same thing to every face?

9.title: First Be Tested
9.context: Tested first, then serve: no instant appointments even for the serving office. The letter does not trust speed in putting people into roles.
9.question: Where would your life or church be healthier if proven-ness were required before promotion?

9.title: Faithful in All Things
9.context: The women of verse 11 are carried as written; the verse has been read as deacons' wives and as women deacons, and the telling takes neither side, only the standard: dignity, bridled speech, temperance, faithfulness.
9.question: How do you handle a text that faithful readers read two ways: with patience or with a need to settle it now?

9.title: Great Confidence in the Faith
9.context: Served well, the tested office yields standing and great confidence, boldness, in the faith. Service turns out to be a road to assurance.
9.question: What unglamorous service in your past built the most confidence in your faith?

10.title: Pillar and Foundation of the Truth
10.context: The letter exists because of a possible delay. Its identity words for the church: God's household, the church of the living God, the pillar and foundation of the truth.
10.question: Which of the three identity pictures, household, church of the living God, pillar, most shapes how you behave among believers?

10.title: He Appeared in the Flesh
10.context: The six-line confession runs incarnation to ascension and out to the nations. The conduct chapters flow from it, and the framing paragraphs ride this scene.
10.question: Which line of the confession do you lean on most, and which have you thought about least?

11.title: The Spirit Expressly States
11.context: Some will abandon the faith in later times, with no timetable built, and the channel is hypocritical liars with seared consciences. Strictness is the tell.
11.question: Where have you mistaken strictness for holiness, in yourself or in a teacher?

11.title: Received with Thanksgiving
11.context: Marriage and foods are defended from creation's goodness: nothing received with thanksgiving should be rejected, sanctified by the word of God and prayer.
11.question: What created good have you been refusing in God's name that gratitude would restore?

11.title: Train Yourself for Godliness
11.context: A good servant is nourished first, then points things out. Myths are refused; training is prescribed, godliness outvaluing bodily exercise because it promises for both lives.
11.question: What would training, not just trying, look like for the godliness you say you want?

11.title: Our Hope on the Living God
11.context: Labor and striving run on hope set on the living God, Savior of everyone, and especially of those who believe, carried as written with no system built on the pairing.
11.question: Is your striving powered by hope, or by fear of what happens if you stop?

12.title: An Example in Five Fields
12.context: Despised youth is answered by example set in speech, conduct, love, faith, and purity. Youth cannot be argued away; it can be outlived in public.
12.question: In which of the five fields is your example currently weakest, and who sees it daily?

12.title: The Public Reading of Scripture
12.context: Reading aloud, exhortation, teaching, in that order, stand at the center of the interim work. A church fed by read Scripture is harder to feed myths.
12.question: When did hearing Scripture read aloud, not studied alone, last change something in you?

12.title: Do Not Neglect the Gift
12.context: The gift came through prophecy at the laying on of the elders' hands, and its named danger is neglect. Diligence and absorption promise progress evident to all.
12.question: What gift in you is currently endangered less by opposition than by neglect?

12.title: Save Yourself and Your Hearers
12.context: Life and teaching are watched as a pair, and perseverance in them is tied, as the letter states it, to saving both the teacher and those who hear.
12.question: Which needs your closer attention this month, your life or your teaching, and what is the first act of attention?

13.title: As to a Father, as Mothers, as Sisters
13.context: Correction in God's household carries the relationship inside it: appeal to the older, family words for every age, absolute purity guarding the young leader.
13.question: Whom do you need to correct, and what would appealing as to family sound like instead?

13.title: Worse Than an Unbeliever
13.context: Family responsibility comes first, repayment as godliness at home; the truly alone widow hopes in God night and day; and the neglect sentence stands at full strength as written.
13.question: What household duty of care is currently unpaid in your life, and to whom?

13.title: Well Known for Good Deeds
13.context: Enrollment requires sixty years, faithfulness, and a reputation made of deeds: children raised, strangers housed, feet washed, the afflicted relieved. A ministry biography answers with support.
13.question: If your good deeds were listed by those who know you best, what would the list honestly contain?

13.title: So That the Truly Alone Are Reached
13.context: The younger-widow counsel and its reasons are carried as Paul gives them, ending in the burden principle: care sorted by truth so the church can reach the widows truly in need.
13.question: Where do you need to sort your care more honestly so the truly needy in your reach are truly reached?

14.title: The Worker Is Worthy of His Wages
14.context: Double honor for elders who lead well, grounded in two sayings Paul cites as Scripture, the ox law and the Lord's word, side by side: the worker fed by the work.
14.question: Are the people who feed you spiritually being honored materially, and what would double honor look like?

14.title: Protected and Exposed
14.context: Unproven charges are not even entertained without two or three witnesses; persistent sin is rebuked in front of everyone. Both halves belong to the honor.
14.question: Is your instinct to protect leaders or expose them, and what would keeping both halves look like?

14.title: Without Bias, Not Too Quick
14.context: The impartiality charge is sworn before God, Christ Jesus, and the elect angels. Hasty ordination makes the ordainer a shareholder in later sins.
14.question: What decision are you being rushed into that slowness would purify?

14.title: Some Records Arrive Late
14.context: The wine note is carried plainly as personal counsel to a frequently ill man. The close governs all the chapter's sorting: sins and good deeds both surface on their own schedules, which is why the letter prescribes time.
14.question: What are you judging too early in someone, before their record has had time to surface?

15.title: Teach and Encourage These Principles
15.context: The slavery passage is carried as written in its setting, its stated aim the protection of God's name and the teaching from discredit, with brotherhood used as a reason for devotion.
15.question: Where might your conduct discredit the teaching you claim, in the eyes of people watching your household?

15.title: Godliness as a Means of Gain
15.context: The last false-teacher portrait: conceit with ignorance, appetite for controversy, a harvest of friction, and the root exposed, religion monetized.
15.question: Have you ever been tempted to make faith useful for gain, and what did the temptation promise?

15.title: Food and Clothing
15.context: Gain exists: godliness with contentment. Nothing in, nothing out, and sufficiency defined low on purpose, contentment as doctrine, not temperament.
15.question: What is your honest definition of enough, and how does it compare with food and clothing?

15.title: The Root of All Kinds of Evil
15.context: The snare is wanting to be rich, and the famous sentence is carried in its exact words, the love of money, all kinds of evil, the damage at the end self-inflicted.
15.question: Where is wanting, rather than having, currently doing the damage in your life?

16.title: Flee and Pursue
16.context: Man of God, Moses' and the prophets' title, is laid on Timothy at the fleeing point: away from craving, toward righteousness, godliness, faith, love, perseverance, gentleness.
16.question: What are you running from, and what are you running toward, stated in one sentence each?

16.title: Take Hold of the Eternal Life
16.context: The good fight returns with a grip: take hold of the eternal life tied to Timothy's own good confession before many witnesses.
16.question: What public confession of yours needs to be fought on the strength of, the way Paul uses Timothy's?

16.title: Before Pontius Pilate
16.context: Timothy's confession is set beside Christ's confession before Pilate exactly as Paul sets them, and the keeping is dated to the appearance, in God's own time, with no timetable given.
16.question: What are you keeping without stain that only endurance, not speed, can finish?

16.title: Unapproachable Light
16.context: Alone immortal, dwelling in unapproachable light, unseen and unseeable: honor and eternal dominion, Amen. Paul cannot command for long before he worships.
16.question: Does your work tend to interrupt your worship, or your worship your work, and which needs the interruption?

17.title: Rich in the Present Age
17.context: Wealth is indexed to this age only; its dangers are conceit and misplaced hope; and God richly provides all things for us to enjoy, enjoyment included in the instruction.
17.question: Is your hope parked in wealth's uncertainty or in the God who provides, and what evidence settles it?

17.title: That Which Is Truly Life
17.context: Rich in good works, generous and ready to share, treasuring up a firm foundation: their own banking instinct re-aimed at the future that matters.
17.question: What deposit could you make this week toward the foundation that is truly life?

17.title: Guard What Has Been Entrusted
17.context: The deposit language of the whole letter lands as a job description. The so-called knowledge's label is Paul's own, and its professors swerved, the letter's first diagnosis completing its circle.
17.question: What has been entrusted to you that you are currently guarding least carefully?

17.title: Grace Be with You All
17.context: The letter to one man ends by blessing the whole church he serves, plural as written.
17.question: Whom does your private obedience quietly bless beyond yourself?
